title: Ref
description:
A named reference to a commit, carrying a valuation overlay.

The valuation overlay is how forks-as-valuation-overlays work on the
persistent store: creating a ref is O(1) (a pointer + an overlay), and
evaluating it is O(dependent slice) through the support index. The base
commit's fact set is unchanged; the overlay just re-values event variables
at query time — exactly the `dli_eval::ForkStore` model, made durable.

authority.description: The authority owning this ref (unset in sovereign deployments).

commit.description: The commit this ref points to.

schema_version.description: Schema version; bumped when the stored shape changes.

valuation.description:
The valuation overlay: event variables ruled true or false by this ref.
Applied over the commit's base valuation at evaluation time.

Authority.description:
The authority that asserted an object.

Exists on every stored object; stays `None` in single-sovereign
deployments (DEF-4 unchanged). In multi-authority configurations, the
authority tag distinguishes who proposed or ruled the object — and because
it participates in the content hash, the same proposition asserted by two
authorities is two distinct objects, never conflated by dedup.

ContentHash.description: A `sha256:<hex>` content digest of a JCS-serialized object.

Valuation.description: A (possibly partial) assignment of truth values to atoms.
